message.content:
The quadratic equation  

\[
3x^{2}-2x-5=0
\]

can be solved with the quadratic formula \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}\).

Here \(a=3,\; b=-2,\; c=-5\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
x &= \frac{-(-2)\pm\sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4(3)(-5)}}{2(3)} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{4+60}}{6} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm\sqrt{64}}{6} \\
  &= \frac{2\pm 8}{6}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the two roots are

\[
x_1 = \frac{2+8}{6} = \frac{10}{6} = \frac{5}{3}, \qquad
x_2 = \frac{2-8}{6} = \frac{-6}{6} = -1.
\]

So the solutions are \(\boxed{x=\frac{5}{3}\text{ or }x=-1}\).
message.reasoning: We need to solve quadratic 3x^2 - 2x - 5 = 0. Use quadratic formula: x = [2 ± sqrt(4 + 60)]/(6) = [2 ± sqrt64]/6 = [2 ± 8]/6. So roots: (2+8)/6 = 10/6 = 5/3; (2-8)/6 = -6/6 = -1. So roots: x = 5/3 and x = -1. Provide answer. No tool needed.
